MOBILITY PROGRAMME FOR ENTITIES INVOLVED IN THE
DEVELOPMENT AND USE OF KISWAHILI IN THE EAC
1. Background
The East African Kiswahili Commission (EAKC) is an institution of the East African
Community (EAC) mandate to coordinate and promote the use of Kiswahili for regional
integration and sustainable development. The Commission collaborates and works in partnership
with Kiswahili stakeholders in executing its mandate in EAC Partner States of Burundi, Kenya,
Rwanda, South Sudan, Uganda and the United Republic of Tanzania. Challenges facing the
language in the EAC region have increased dramatically in recent years as witnessed in the
phenomenal growth and complexity of the number of entities involved in its development and
use. Many of the entities often lack the full complement of staff needed to operate their
programmes, invariably adversely impacting on their effectiveness and efficiency, and affecting
the quality of their products/outcomes. There is need to bring together Kiswahili stakeholders in
order to strengthen joint action to address these and other emerging issues. Mobility is, therefore,
an integral part of the overall purpose, strategy and organization of the Commission as it is
considered critical in strengthening and helping build capacity. Mobility of Kiswahili
stakeholders is very important in helping the Commission achieve its strategic objective of
coordinating and harmonizing the development and use of Kiswahili. This Mobility Programme,
therefore, is part of the Commission’s drive to develop institutional strategies, concrete
initiatives and support structures to enhance this process whose aim is to create opportunities for
highly dynamic partnerships and linkages for nurturing skills and competencies of Kiswahili
stakeholders in East Africa.
The East African Community recognizes Kiswahili as an important asset and resource in the
integration process and sustainable economic, political and social development of the
Community.
2. Objective
The objective of the Mobility Programme is to provide opportunities for Kiswahili stakeholders
to interact in a creative and innovative manner so as to establish strategic partnerships,
sustainable collaborations and strong and broad co-operation as a means towards the
development and use of Kiswahili for regional integration and sustainable development.
1

3. Scope of the Programme
This Mobility Programme applies to Kiswahili stakeholders in the EAC. Among stakeholders
targeted in this Programme are the following:
i) Individuals engaged in the development and use of Kiswahili in EAC Partner
States;
ii) Groups of Kiswahili stakeholders in EAC Partner States;
iii) Institutions dealing with Kiswahili in EAC Partner States;
4. Programme Activities
Strategic priority areas for the Mobility Programme include, but are not limited to, the following:
4.1 Study Visits;
4.2 Collaborative research;
4.3 Teaching;
4.4 Graduate theses supervision;
4.5 Course review, evaluation and design;
4.6 External Examination;
4.7 Internship/Field Attachment;
4.8 Mentorship;
4.9 Writing;
4.10 Practicum;
4.11 Short Fellowship;
4.12 Study tours;
4.13 Volunteering;
4.14 Short courses;
4.15 Placements;
4.16 Guest Talks;
4.17 Exchanges;
4.18 In-service training.
5. Expected Outcomes and Impact
The Commission has developed this Programme as a common strategy and process with the aim
of facilitating exchanges and encouraging networking among Kiswahili stakeholders in East
Africa and beyond. It is expected that upon successful completion, the following will be realized:
Ø Professional development of the participant and on both sending and receving entity;
Ø Improved knowledge and skills;
Ø Innovative learning;
Ø Enhanced intercultural awareness;
Ø Provision of new skills, motivation, fresh outlook and perspectives and an expanded
network;
Ø Strengthening of the spirit of regional integration in the EAC;
Ø Exposure to different environments, perspectives and ways of developing and using
Kiswahili;
Ø Become more effective and efficient in the development and use of Kiswahili;
Ø Establishment of meaningful cooperative partnerships, linkages and collaborations;
2

6. Criteria and Conditions
To qualify to participate in the Programme, individuals, a group of people and institutions must:
i) Be actively involved in the development and use of Kiswahili in an AEC Partner
State;
ii) Be an active member with the East African Kiswahili Commission;
iii) Be nominated and recommended to the Commission by a known Kiswahili
stakeholder;
iv) Have a clear proposal of what activity is to be undertaken;
v) Have a plan developed and approved by their respective authorities;
vi) Be in a position to meet any other requirements stipulated by the Commission and/or
the host institution/provider;
vii) Any other criterion that may be considered and approved for application by the
Commission and both the sending and host institutions.
The Commission may arrange for an interview where it deems necessary.
7. Organization and Financing of the Programme
The administration of the Mobility Programme is the responsibility of the East African Kiswahili
Commission in collaboration with participating partners and stakeholders. The Commission will
offer opportunities to support innovative initiatives and links by stakeholders who wish to
undertake a collaborative activity. The Commission will provide a modest fund for any of the
above identified priority areas, allocate resources and select qualified candidates. The
Commission will be in charge of coordinating the linkages and networks and running the projects
together with respective partner institutions.
Participants may be entitled to other benefits as determined by their institutions.
8. Timeframe
i) Announcement Date: 4th March, 2019
ii) Application Deadline: 5th April, 2019
iii) Commencement Date: 1st June, 2019
iv) Duration: Varies but not more than THREE Months.

7. COMMITTEMNT BY THE FOUR PARTIES
a) East African Kiswahili Commission
i. Facilitate travel of the applicant from sending institution to host institution.
ii. Pay a modest allowance commensurate to applicant’s qualification, institution and
duration to comfortably participate in the mobility programme.
iii. Refund Travel Insurance not exceeding USD 150.
iv. Acknowledge and Certify Applicant’s successful participation in the Mobility
Programme.
b) Applicant
i. Fill and submit complete application within specified deadline.
ii. Adhere to programme of activities agreed between the Commission, sending
Institution and Host Institution.
iii. File a report to the Commission on the Mobility exercise.
iv. Secure a Travel Insurance not exceeding USD 150.
7

c) Sending Institution
i. To nominate and endorse the applicant for the Mobility Programme.
ii. To retain the applicant’s benefits during the duration of the Mobility activity.
d) Host Institution
i. Qualify as an entity that develops and uses Kiswahili.
ii. Apply to the East African Kiswahili Commission for consideration to play host.
iii. Propose Calendar of activities after the applicant has been nominated and
accepted.
iv. Provide appropriate accommodation.
v. Arrange for pick-up and drop-off of applicant on arrival and departure
respectively.
vi. Provide furnished working space for the applicant for the duration of the exercise.
vii. Accord any other support and extend necessary courtesies to the applicant for
their comfort, safety and security.
